'''Urs Paul Rolf Wild''' (17 April 1936 – 22 November 2022)<ref>{{cite web |title=Urs Paul Rolf Wild death notice |url=https://trauer.nzz.ch/traueranzeige/urs-paul-rolf-wild |website=rauer.nzz.ch |access-date=30 November 2022 |date=29 November 2022}}</ref> was a Swiss chemist. He became known for his pioneering works in [[Single-molecule experiment|single molecule detection]].

==Biography==
Wild studied chemistry at [[ETH Zurich]]. He received his Master Diploma in physics at the [[University of Kansas]], Lawrence, Kansas, US, in 1962. He completed his PhD under Professor Günthard at the Laboratory of Physical Chemistry, ETH Zurich in 1965, the subject of his PhD thesis was "Aufbau einer Blitzlichtapparatur mit Zündfunkenstrecke und ihre Anwendung zum Studium der Triplett-Triplett Annihilation von Anthracen in Glycerin".<ref>[https://www.research-collection.ethz.ch/handle/20.500.11850/136341?show=full ETH Zurich Research Collection]</ref>

In 1972 Wild was appointed assistant professor at the Laboratory of Physical Chemistry, ETH Zurich. He was promoted to associate professor in 1977 and to full professor in 1984. He retired in October 2001.<ref>[https://ethz.ch/en/the-eth-zurich/organisation/who-is-who/retired-professors/details.NzgxMTc=.TGlzdC80MDEsMTk1NzY4MzcwOQ==.html Wild, Urs, Prof. em. Dr.]</ref>

From 2000 Wild was a member of [[Heidelberg Academy of Sciences and Humanities]].<ref>[http://www.haw.uni-heidelberg.de/akademie/member.en.html?id=232 List of members of Heidelberger Science Academy]</ref>

He worked with, among others, the Polish physical chemist {{ill|Jerzy Sepioł|pl}}.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Google Scholar |url=https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=pl&as_sdt=0,5&q=sepio%C5%82+wild&btnG= |access-date=2022-07-16 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>

[[William E. Moerner]] took an eight-month sabbatical in 1993–1994 to become a visiting guest professor in the lab of Wild at ETH Zurich, Switzerland.<ref>[https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/chemistry/2014/moerner/biographical/ William E. Moerner Biographical]</ref>
